newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine soybean crop 11 to 12 mln T - traders.
newsitem.headline: Argentine soybean crop 11 to 12 mln T - traders.

text.p: Argentine traders' forecasts for soybean output differed widely Thursday, with estimates ranging from 11 million to 12 million tonnes.
But traders were mostly nonplussed by market-moving rumors in Chicago that an Argentine firm had lowered its forecast of output to 11 million tonnes from 11.5 million tonnes.

"They're long on beans. They obviously need to sell beans," was one reaction. The trader added, "We're sticking to 12 million tonnes. For the moment we see no reason to change. Some areas are better than normal, but most are worse than normal. Eleven million tonnes is out of the question. That's ridiculous."
He also said that the government's Agriculture Secretariat's official forecast of 12.9 million tonnes, was "ridiculous also."
But a second trader said that he had been at 11 million tonnes for weeks, due to damage from a long drought: "I'd say 11 million is fair enough. I wouldn't say that I'd lower it any more."
Other traders consulted by Reuters were scattered between 11 million and 12 million tonnes.
The U.S. Agricultural Department said earier in April that it predicted 13.25 million tonnes.
Rosario-based brokers Enrique Zeni forecast 11.3 million tonnes last week, higher than the 10.5 million tonnes forecast by fellow brokers Guardatti-Torti.

Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola said last Wednesday that the only forecasts worth listening to were the Argentine government's and the USDA's, as they were the only ones with big teams studying the crops.
The government said in its weekly crop report Wednesday that 30.8 percent of the soybean crop had been harvested by April 18.
